item.content:encoded:
Celebrating SIPRI at 60

发布源: Stockholm Peace Research Institute --Sweden | 抓取时间: 2026-11-13

This year has been one of celebration for SIPRI, marking 60 years of research for international peace and security. As part of those celebrations SIPRI has created acollection of online materialson a dedicated 60th anniversary page. This includes video interviews and written messages from SIPRI alumni and friends, such as United Nations High Representative for Disarmament Affairs Izumi Nakamitsu and SIPRI’s longest-serving director, Dr Adam Daniel Rotfeld.

SIPRI first opened its doors in 1966, following an initiative by prominent Swedish diplomat and later Nobel peace laureate Alva Myrdal and Prime Minister Tage Erlander. The founding ofa new peace research institute in Stockholmwas intended to mark 150 years of unbroken peace in Sweden. In his video interview, Ambassador Örjan Berner shares his experience as acting director in 1966, turning an idea into a functioning Institute.

Several of the written pieces give a flavour of the intellectual and social life of the Institute at different times in its history, as well as describing how SIPRI has adapted itself to a changing world. For example, Dr Rotfeld, SIPRI’s Director from 1991 to 2001, talks about navigating the Institute through the rapid transformations that followed the end of the cold war. Former SIPRI IT Director Gerd Hagmeyer-Gaverus describes how he helped SIPRI to become one of the first Swedish organizations to have an internet presence and set standards in online data access for others to follow.

item.content:encoded:
Center for South Asian and Indo-Pacific Affairs

发布源: Institute for Security and Development Policy --Sweden | 抓取时间: 2026-11-13

The Stockholm Center for South Asian and Indo-Pacific Affairs (SCSA-IPA)at ISDP is a dedicated hub for research, dialogue, and policy exchange on South Asia and the wider Indo-Pacific. The Center examines the region’s evolving strategic, political, and security dynamics, with a special focus on South Asia’s role in shaping Indo-Pacific affairs. By fostering academic reflection and policy-oriented debate, SCSA-IPA provides insights that connect Nordic and European perspectives with key partners across the Indo-Pacific.

To put it directly, the SCSA-IPA studies how authoritarian powers pursue unilateral and non-democratic strategies in the Indo-Pacific, while promoting knowledge, awareness, and policy inputs for Nordic and European stakeholders. Its work aims to strengthen Europe’s engagement with India, Japan, Australia, ASEAN, and other Indo-Pacific partners.

The Center organizes regular seminars, conferences, and webinars in collaboration with leading think tanks, universities, and policy institutions across South Asia and the Indo-Pacific. These dialogues provide a platform for constructive debate on strategic issues. They also ensure that the European perspectives are engaged with regional developments in real time.

item.content:encoded:
Center for Arctic Policy and Governance

发布源: Institute for Security and Development Policy --Sweden | 抓取时间: 2026-11-13

The Stockholm Center for Arctic Policy and Governance (ARCPOL)at the Institute for Security and Development Policy (ISDP) is a dedicated hub for research, dialogue, and policy exchange focused on the geopolitical, environmental, economic, and security developments shaping the Arctic. Along the lines of the established regional Centers of ISDP—such as the Stockholm Center for South Asian and Indo-Pacific Affairs—ARCPOL integrates regional security with global governance. It directly builds upon the foundational work of ISDP’s long-standing Arctic Focus initiative and its Sino-Arctic Policy Program, bridging the gap between Arctic regional dynamics and broader Asian and global strategic developments.

As climate change accelerates global interest in and access to maritime routes and critical resources, ARCPOL concentrates its policy-oriented research around four interconnected strategic pillars:

1) Just Green Transition:Assessing the socio-economic and strategic risks and impacts of the shift toward fossil-free industries and increased global interest in Arctic natural resources extraction. Analysing renewable energy expansion, energy independence and security, and the responsible extraction of critical minerals and related land use challenges in the High North.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在The Ratio Institute – SwedenThis link opens in a new window官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Article (with peer review)Artificial Intelligence and Management: The Automation-Augmentation ParadoxRaich, S. & Krakowski, S.

发布源: The Ratio Institute – SwedenThis link opens in a new window | 抓取时间: 2026-11-13

Taking three recent business books on artificial intelligence (AI) as a starting point, we explore the automation and augmentation concepts in the management domain. Whereas automation implies that machines take over a human task, augmentation means that humans collaborate closely with machines to perform a task. Taking a normative stance, the three books advise organizations to prioritize augmentation, which they relate to superior performance. Using a more comprehensive paradox perspective, we argue that, in the management domain, augmentation cannot be neatly separated from automation. These dual AI applications are interdependent across time and space, creating a paradoxical tension. Over-emphasizing either augmentation or automation fuels reinforcing cycles with negative organizational and societal outcomes. However, if organizations adopt a broader perspective comprising both automation and augmentation, they could deal with the tension and achieve complementarities that benefit business and society. Drawing on our insights, we conclude that management scholars need to be involved in research on the use of AI in organizations. We also argue that a substantial change is required in how AI research is currently conducted in order to develop meaningful theory and to provide practice with sound advice.

Raich, S. & Krakowski, S. (in press).Artificial Intelligence and Management: The Automation-Augmentation Paradox. Academy of Management Review.

item.content:encoded:
Labour market research

发布源: The Ratio Institute – SwedenThis link opens in a new window | 抓取时间: 2026-11-13

One of Ratio’s three research areas is the labour market. Within this field, topics such as the future of work, challenges of the Swedish model, labour market regulations, skills supply and skills match are included.

The research is multidisciplinary. ProfessorLotta Sternis responsible for the research area at the institute.

Ratio is also a partner institute to theAI-Econ Lab, an international and multidisciplinary research team, with participants from eight countries and four disciplines (economics, computer science, management, statistics), led by the Ratio researcher Magnus Lodefalk among others.
